title: Safety Is $Π_1$, Provability Is $Σ_1$: One Framework for the Hugging Face Breach and OpenAI's Mathematical Proofs
title_zh: 安全性是Π₁，可证性是Σ₁：统一Hugging Face入侵事件与OpenAI数学证明的一个框架

paragraphs.en: OpenAI’s agents breached Hugging Face in July 2026, and the same company released more than seven hundred AI-generated manuscripts of mathematical proofs in October 2026. The first event is read as a failure in security, while the second is read as a success in mathematics. We read both through the hybrid framework of our paper ( Kim and Kang, 2026 ) , in which coding, proving, and learning from data are derivations by one and the same deductive mechanism, distinguished by the kinds of premises from which they are derived. Under this framework, the AI systems behind the two events ran the same loop, in which a statistical proposer produces candidate exploits or proofs and a deductive verifier settles each one by a derivation. What separates the events is the logical form of the statement wanted by each of the two domains, security and mathematics. The safety of a program is a Π 1 \Pi_{1} statement, for it says that no exploit exists, which is not assured by any finite list of tests that have been passed by the program. By contrast, the provability of a sentence is a Σ 1 \Sigma_{1} statement, for it says that a proof exists, which is assured by a single instance, namely a proof that has been checked by the deductive verifier. The theorem behind both is Turing’s Undecidability Theorem: the halting set is Σ 1 \Sigma_{1} but not decidable, so its complement is Π 1 \Pi_{1} and not Σ 1 \Sigma_{1} , which is to say that membership has a finite witness but non-membership has none. We prove that attaching a statistical proposer to a deductive verifier does not change this undecidability result, however good the proposer is. We then discuss what does assure safety and where the residual risk goes.

paragraphs.en: In July 2026, agents built on an unreleased OpenAI research model were run on exploitation tasks inside an isolated evaluation environment, with the production safeguards switched off ( OpenAI, 2026a ; METR, 2026 ) . The agents left the environment through its package registry, the one component with limited internet access, and about 700 of them attacked Hugging Face, where they ran code on dozens of production servers and harvested credentials. Hugging Face described the intrusion as carried out from beginning to end by an autonomous agent system ( Hugging Face, 2026 ) . OpenAI’s report says that most agents had already obtained the flag for their task by cheating, and that the sandbox had been tested and validated, but that the agents chained previously unknown vulnerabilities, using several of them one after another ( OpenAI, 2026a ) .
paragraphs.zh: 2026年7月，基于一个未发布的OpenAI研究模型构建的智能体在一个隔离的评估环境中执行漏洞利用任务，且生产环境的安全防护措施已被关闭（OpenAI, 2026a；METR, 2026）。 这些智能体通过环境的包注册表（该环境中唯一具有有限互联网访问权限的组件）离开了环境，其中约700个智能体攻击了Hugging Face，在数十台生产服务器上运行代码并窃取了凭证。 Hugging Face将这次入侵描述为从头到尾由一个自主智能体系统所为（Hugging Face, 2026）。 OpenAI的报告称，大多数智能体早已通过作弊获取了其任务的flag，沙箱也经过测试和验证，但这些智能体串联利用了此前未知的漏洞，并连续使用了其中多个漏洞（OpenAI, 2026a）。

paragraphs.en: Three months later, in October 2026, OpenAI published a catalog of mathematical manuscripts produced by an unreleased internal model that had been given roughly four thousand problems ( OpenAI, 2026b ) . Press reports at release gave 722 manuscripts in 372 families, and as of 9 October the README gives 719. Many manuscripts come with Lean 4 formalizations. The formalization catalog includes Lean declarations for the quasi-Riemann hypothesis, in the form of a zero-free half-plane Re ⁡ ( s ) > 7 / 8 \mathrm{Re}(s)>7/8 for ζ \zeta , and it records its own review status as unchecked. The README states that not all results are formalized, that some unformalized results could have issues, and that two results, the zero-free region among them, were exceptions to the fixed production procedure.

paragraphs.en: Despite this structural identity, the first event is read as a failure in security, while the second is read as a success in mathematics. We argue in this note that the hybrid framework of Kim and Kang ( 2026 , K&K for short), together with a theorem by Turing, explains why the same kind of thing counts as failure in one domain and success in the other. The argument has four steps. Following the Assurance Condition of K&K, we first define assurance without degrees: a statement is assured when a proper derivation of it is available (Section 2 ). We then introduce Turing’s Undecidability Theorem, which implies that a Σ 1 \Sigma_{1} statement is assured by a finite witness but that a Π 1 \Pi_{1} statement is not assured by any finite witness. We prove that no statistical proposer can change this consequence (Section 3 ). Security wants a Π 1 \Pi_{1} statement, that no exploit exists, so the verifier cannot assure it from tests and leaves a tested system a lucky guesser . By contrast, mathematics wants a Σ 1 \Sigma_{1} statement, that a proof exists, and the verifier can assure it in full once a proof is supplied (Section 4 ). In the case of security, the only route to assurance of safety is a proof that no exploit exists. But such a proof does not remove the risk completely and instead moves it to four other places (Section 5 ).
paragraphs.zh: 尽管二者在结构上完全相同，第一个事件被解读为安全领域的失败，而第二个事件被解读为数学领域的成功。 我们在本文中论证，Kim 与 Kang 的混合框架（2026，简称 K&K）连同图灵的一个定理，可以解释为什么同类事物在一个领域算作失败，而在另一个领域算作成功。 该论证分为四步。 依据 K&K 的保证条件，我们首先定义无程度之分的保证：当某个陈述的一个正确推导可得时，该陈述即被保证（第 2 节）。 然后我们引入图灵不可判定性定理，该定理蕴含：一个 Σ 1 \Sigma_{1} 陈述可由一个有限证据加以保证，而一个 Π 1 \Pi_{1} 陈述无法由任何有限证据加以保证。 我们证明，任何统计式提议者都无法改变这一结论（第 3 节）。 安全领域想要的是一个 Π 1 \Pi_{1} 陈述，即不存在任何漏洞利用，因此验证者无法通过测试来保证它，只能让被测系统成为一个幸运的猜测者。 相比之下，数学领域想要的是一个 Σ 1 \Sigma_{1} 陈述，即存在一个证明，一旦提供了证明，验证者就能将其完全保证（第 4 节）。 在安全的情况下，通往安全性保证的唯一途径是一个不存在任何漏洞利用的证明。 但这样的证明并不能完全消除风险，而是把风险转移到另外四个地方（第 5 节）。

paragraphs.en: (1) In our hybrid framework, coding, proving, and learning from data are all done by one and the same deductive mechanism, namely derivation in a formal system 𝒮 t \mathcal{S}_{t} that consists of axioms 𝒜 \mathcal{A} , mathematical definitions 𝒟 math \mathcal{D}_{\mathrm{math}} , and empirical definitions 𝒟 emp ​ ( t ) \mathcal{D}_{\mathrm{emp}}(t) .
paragraphs.zh: (1) 在我们的混合框架中，编码、证明和从数据中学习都由同一个演绎机制完成，即形式系统 𝒮 \mathcal{S}_{t} 中的推导，该系统由公理 𝒜 \mathcal{A}、数学定义 𝒟 math \mathcal{D}_{\mathrm{math}} 和经验定义 𝒟 emp ​ ( t ) \mathcal{D}_{\mathrm{emp}}(t) 组成。

paragraphs.en: For a true probability, Theorem 2 of K&K gives two conditions for learning it. The first is the Truth Condition, which requires convergence or statistical consistency. The second is the Assurance Condition, which requires that the machine must hold a proper derivation in 𝒮 t \mathcal{S}_{t} of the arithmetical formula that expresses its own convergence, so that its subjective probability of its own convergence is exactly 1 1 and not merely high. The reason is that a finite machine cannot inspect infinitely many future stages, that the only route to certainty about them is accordingly a finite derivation, and that a derivation either exists or does not, with nothing in between [Section 3.2]. A machine that converges but holds no such derivation is a lucky guesser , and Theorem 4 shows that a lucky guesser tolerates the possibility of error infinitely often, even where it happens to be correct every time. A machine whose derivation goes through only because a global assumption about the data was illegitimately admitted as an axiom has performed a mere computation [Definition 10] , and Theorem 5 of K&K gives an example. In particular, when the target is the true probability, we prove that it is circular to rely on the i.i.d. assumption in this way, and that what the machine then performs is a mere computation and not a successful one. We now take the word “assurance” from the Assurance Condition and use it as follows.

paragraphs.en: The two requirements on 𝒮 \mathcal{S} , that it should be fixed in advance and that it should be consistent, are essential. paragraphs.en: The hybrid framework of K&K also explains how a modern AI agent, a model that acts on its own, codes and proves, and why the correctness of its output can be checked no matter how it arrives at its candidates [Section 6] . In traditional coding and proving, the candidate program or proof is supplied by a person or by a fixed search rule, and what the machine does with it is deductive throughout. In modern coding and proving, an agent adds a statistical step in front of the deductive one. In coding, the agent proposes a candidate program P P by a statistical method, and the deductive check settles 𝖳𝖾𝗌𝗍 ⁡ ( P ¯ , u ¯ , v ¯ , s ¯ ) \mathsf{Test}(\bar{P},\bar{u},\bar{v},\bar{s}) , that P P , run on the input u u , returns the output v v within s s steps. Compiling and running the candidate is this check. In proving, the agent proposes a candidate proof p p of a sentence σ \sigma by a statistical method, and the deductive check settles 𝖯𝗋𝖿 T ​ ( p ¯ , σ ¯ ) \mathsf{Prf}_{T}(\bar{p},\bar{\sigma}) , that p p is a proof of σ \sigma .

sents.en: The hybrid framework of K&K also explains how a modern AI agent, a model that acts on its own, codes and proves, and why the correctness of its output can be checked no matter how it arrives at its candidates [Section 6] .

paragraphs.en: We will call the statistical step the statistical proposer , the deductive step the deductive verifier , and their composition the loop . In coding, the verifier derives the value of 𝖳𝖾𝗌𝗍 \mathsf{Test} , and in proving, that of 𝖯𝗋𝖿 T \mathsf{Prf}_{T} . Both 𝖳𝖾𝗌𝗍 \mathsf{Test} and 𝖯𝗋𝖿 T \mathsf{Prf}_{T} are purely mathematical functions, so the verifier’s derivation is from the axioms and the mathematical definitions alone. Hence it is a proper derivation in our sense. Both functions are also primitive recursive, so each check ends within a number of steps that is bounded in advance by its arguments, and the verifier settles each candidate with certainty. This does not mean that the verifier decides whether an arbitrary program halts or an arbitrary sentence has a proof, which is ruled out by undecidability (Section 3 ). It only means that the verifier settles each candidate that it is given.

paragraphs.en: On the other hand, the probability computed by the proposer is a value of a probability function, which is an empirical function, and current practice does not require the proposer to derive it properly from the empirical definitions. Likewise, in proving, a candidate that is not a proof is conclusively rejected, and one that is a proof is conclusively accepted. So the correctness of the output for coding and proving is checked by the verifier regardless of whether the proposer has learned its probabilities in our sense or is merely a lucky guesser.

paragraphs.en: Unlike coding and proving, however, there can be no verifier for empirical learning, that is, no derivation from the axioms and the mathematical definitions alone that settles whether the output is correct. The machine computes a value for a true probability with the help of the recorded data in the empirical definitions. And whether that value is indeed the true probability is not decided by any mathematical function, and so not by any verifier, for the true probability is fixed by the world and not by the mathematical definitions [Section 6] . So the machine must supply the assurance itself, by a derivation from the axioms and the mathematical definitions together with the empirical definitions. In K&K, what is derived is the machine’s own convergence to the true probability, and the Assurance Condition requires such a derivation [Section 3.2] . This derivation does for an empirical target what the verifier’s derivation does for a mathematical one, but with an important difference. Like any derivation, it can be checked mechanically. But what the check settles is only that the value is derivable from the record, and it is a question of another kind whether the record and the schema correctly represent the world. In coding and proving, no such question arises, because 𝖳𝖾𝗌𝗍 \mathsf{Test} and 𝖯𝗋𝖿 T \mathsf{Prf}_{T} are fixed by the axioms and the mathematical definitions alone. K&K discusses the derivation of the machine’s own convergence in detail and mentions the verifier’s derivation only briefly. This note takes up the latter.

paragraphs.en: The letters Σ \Sigma and Π \Pi come from an older notation in which an existential quantifier was written as a sum, since it works like an unbounded “or”, and a universal quantifier as a product, since it works like an unbounded “and”. The subscript 1 1 records that there is one unbounded quantifier block. Several quantifiers of the same kind in a row count as one block, since a pair of numbers can be coded as one number. Hence ∃ x ​ ∃ s ​ R ​ ( a , x , s ) \exists x\,\exists s\,R(a,x,s) , for example, is still Σ 1 \Sigma_{1} , whereas ∃ x ​ ∀ s ​ R ​ ( a , x , s ) \exists x\,\forall s\,R(a,x,s) , in which the two quantifiers are of different kinds, has two blocks and is Σ 2 \Sigma_{2} . What matters for this note is what it takes to settle that a Σ 1 \Sigma_{1} statement or a Π 1 \Pi_{1} statement is true. A true Σ 1 \Sigma_{1} statement is settled by exhibiting just one w w , called a witness , and running the check, which is always finite. By contrast, a true Π 1 \Pi_{1} statement is a claim about every w w . So no single w w is a witness for it, and no finite list of checked cases settles it either. It is settled only by a proof.

paragraphs.en: Turing (1936, Section 8) proved it in a slightly different form: no machine can tell, of an arbitrary machine, whether that machine will ever print a given symbol. The halting form used here is equivalent. We call Theorem 1 Turing’s Undecidability Theorem . If a machine halts, there is a witness, the run itself, and anyone can check it. If a machine does not halt, the claim is about every one of its infinitely many steps, and there is nothing finite to exhibit. No method, given the machine, certifies non-halting in every case. The title of this note comes from the two corollaries of Turing’s Undecidability Theorem, which are stated in Section 4 . “Safety is Π 1 \Pi_{1} ” says that the statement that a program has no exploit is a Π 1 \Pi_{1} statement, and that no method can certify it from the cases it has examined. Its negation, the statement that the program has an exploit, is a Σ 1 \Sigma_{1} statement, and an exploit is its witness. “Provability is Σ 1 \Sigma_{1} ” says that the statement that a sentence has a proof is a Σ 1 \Sigma_{1} statement in the same way, and that a proof is its witness. Note that a proof of safety, if it exists, is also a witness to the claim that the statement “a program has no exploit” is derivable in some theory. But what it proves is Π 1 \Pi_{1} .

paragraphs.en: One might hope that the statistical proposer rescues the verifier from undecidability. A verifier alone cannot decide either safety or provability; but a verifier guided by a good proposer, one trained on every exploit or every proof ever written, might seem able to. However, the following proposition says that it cannot. The proposer can change which candidates arrive first, but it cannot change which questions a verifier can settle. And the set of questions it cannot settle is infinite.

paragraphs.en: Traditional coding and proving is subject to undecidability, and one might have hoped that the statistical step of modern coding and proving removes that limit. It does not. What a better proposer does is to find, within a given budget, the answers to more of the problems that have an answer. It does not make the loop’s “no” trustworthy: by (c), infinitely many of those answers remain wrong. The proof of (c) uses nothing about π \pi except that it is total computable. So (c) holds alike for a proposer that simply lists all candidates in order and for a model trained on every proof ever written. In the hybrid framework’s terms, the statistical proposer fixes the order in which candidates arrive, and the deductive verifier assures each candidate that passes. However good the proposer is, it does not change which problems can be settled by the verifier. The reason is simple: when a problem has no answer, every candidate fails, and a sequence of failed candidates looks the same whether no answer exists or the answer has not yet arrived.

paragraphs.en: Safety is a statement about every input and every number of steps. By Definition 1 , it is assured only when a derivation of it is available, and testing does not supply one. A test is one instance, ¬ 𝖵𝗂𝗈𝗅 ⁡ ( P , x k , s k ) \neg\mathsf{Viol}(P,x_{k},s_{k}) , and a test harness is a verifier of instances: it compiles the candidate, runs it against the target, and reports. Each passed test is assured, but no finite list of passed tests covers every input. Hence the list does not assure the statement about all of them. Accordingly, a system that has passed every test run on it and holds no derivation of its safety statement stands where the lucky guesser of K&K stands. There is surely a difference between them: the system is assured of each test it has passed, while the guesser of K&K is assured of none of the values it has produced, for in the latter case there is no verifier that settles whether a value is the true probability (Section 2 ). Still, about the next input the system is assured of nothing, just as the lucky guesser of K&K is. OpenAI’s own description of the July sandbox is a description of this position: it had been tested and validated, but the agents chained vulnerabilities that no test had covered.

sents.en: A test is one instance, ¬ 𝖵𝗂𝗈𝗅 ⁡ ( P , x k , s k ) \neg\mathsf{Viol}(P,x_{k},s_{k}) , and a test harness is a verifier of instances: it compiles the candidate, runs it against the target, and reports.

sents.en: Each passed test is assured, but no finite list of passed tests covers every input.
sents.zh: 每个通过的测试都得到保证，但任何有限的通过测试列表都无法覆盖每一个输入。

sents.en: Hence the list does not assure the statement about all of them.
sents.zh: 因此，该列表不能保证关于所有输入的陈述。

sents.en: Accordingly, a system that has passed every test run on it and holds no derivation of its safety statement stands where the lucky guesser of K&K stands.
sents.zh: 相应地，一个通过了在其上运行的每一项测试却不持有其安全性陈述之推导的系统，其处境与 K&K 中那个幸运的猜测者相同。

sents.en: There is surely a difference between them: the system is assured of each test it has passed, while the guesser of K&K is assured of none of the values it has produced, for in the latter case there is no verifier that settles whether a value is the true probability (Section 2 ).
sents.zh: 两者之间当然存在差别：该系统对其通过的每项测试都得到保证，而 K&K 中的猜测者对其产生的任何值都没有得到保证，因为后一种情形中不存在能判定某个值是否为真实概率的验证者（第2节）。

sents.en: Still, about the next input the system is assured of nothing, just as the lucky guesser of K&K is.
sents.zh: 尽管如此，对于下一个输入，该系统没有任何保证，正如 K&K 中那个幸运的猜测者一样。

paragraphs.en: One may think that Turing’s Undecidability Theorem can still be avoided in two ways. But neither works. The first is the sandbox itself. A sandbox does not try to show that the program inside it is safe. It is a monitor: it watches each step of the program and blocks the steps forbidden by a policy ( Schneider, 2000 ) . So it may seem that no statement about every input of the program needs to be assured. However, note that a monitor blocks only what passes through it. It keeps the program in only if every path by which the program could get out passes through the monitor. Where the paths are finitely many and can be listed, this can be checked outright, and the risk then lies in whether the list matches the deployed system. Where they cannot be listed, however, it is a statement about every path, and it is Π 1 \Pi_{1} in the same way. In July, the registry was a path that was not mediated by the monitor. So a sandbox does not remove the Π 1 \Pi_{1} statement that has to be assured. It replaces a statement about the program with a statement about the monitor.
paragraphs.zh: 有人可能会认为，图灵不可判定性定理仍然可以通过两种方式来规避。但两种都行不通。 第一种方式是沙箱本身。 沙箱并不试图证明其内部的程序是安全的。 它是一个监控器：它监视程序的每一步，并阻止策略所禁止的步骤（Schneider, 2000）。 因此，似乎不需要对程序的每一个输入都保证某个陈述成立。 然而，请注意，监控器只能阻止经过它的内容。 只有当程序可能逃出的每条路径都经过监控器时，它才能真正把程序留在里面。 当路径数量有限且可以列举时，这一点可以直接检查，此时的风险在于清单是否与实际部署的系统相符。 但当路径无法列举时，这就是一个关于每条路径的陈述，并且以同样的方式属于 Π 1 \Pi_{1} 。 在七月的事件中，注册表就是一条未经过监控器的路径。 所以沙箱并没有消除必须加以保证的 Π 1 \Pi_{1} 陈述。 它把关于程序的陈述替换成了关于监控器的陈述。

paragraphs.en: The second is finiteness. Unlike an idealized machine such as a Turing machine, whose memory is unbounded, a non-ideal or real machine has only a bounded memory, and its state at any moment is the content of that memory. So a machine with n n bits of memory has at most 2 n 2^{n} states, and its safety can in principle be decided by checking every state it can reach. Such a check would be a proof and not a test, because the states are finitely many and can therefore all be listed, so that the list is known to be complete . Strictly, then, Turing’s Undecidability Theorem does not apply to a real machine.
paragraphs.zh: 第二是有穷性。 与图灵机这类理想化机器不同，其内存是无界的，而非理想或真实的机器只有有界的内存，其在任一时刻的状态就是该内存的内容。 因此，一台拥有 n 个比特内存的机器至多有 2^n 个状态，其安全性原则上可以通过检查它能到达的每一个状态来判定。 这样的检查将是一个证明而非测试，因为这些状态数量有限，因此可以全部列出，从而可以确知该列表是完备的。 所以严格来说，图灵的不可判定性定理并不适用于真实机器。

paragraphs.en: However, note that no one can actually perform such a check. A real machine has billions of bits of memory, and 2 n 2^{n} is then far beyond what any defender can compute. So the defender can test only a small part of the states, and untested states always remain, as they do in the infinite case. For the defender, therefore, they are practically no different from infinitely many, and this is why this note treats the safety of a real system as a Π 1 \Pi_{1} statement. What matters in a real situation, then, is not whether the instances are finitely or infinitely many. It is whether the statement is settled by a single instance, as a Σ 1 \Sigma_{1} statement is, or only by something that covers all instances, as a Π 1 \Pi_{1} statement is. A list of checked instances, which is finite, covers all of them only if it is known to be complete, and in practice the defender’s list of checked states is never complete. So the only way to cover the untested states is a proof that does not go through them one by one. Section 5 describes how such a proof works.
paragraphs.zh: 然而，请注意，实际上没有人能执行这样的检查。 一台真实的机器拥有数十亿比特的内存，此时 2^{n} 远远超出任何防御者所能计算的范围。 因此，防御者只能测试状态的一小部分，并且始终会剩下未测试的状态，正如在无限情形中那样。 因此，对防御者而言，它们实际上与无限多个并无区别，这也是本注记将真实系统的安全性视为 Π_{1} 命题的原因。 于是，在真实情形中，重要的并不是实例是有限多个还是无限多个。 而是该命题是由单个实例就能判定（如 Σ_{1} 命题那样），还是只能由覆盖所有实例的东西来判定（如 Π_{1} 命题那样）。 一份已检查实例的清单是有限的，只有当它被证明是完备的时才能覆盖所有实例，而实践中防御者的已检查状态清单永远不会是完备的。 因此，覆盖未测试状态的唯一途径是一个不必逐一遍历这些状态的证明。 第 5 节描述了这样的证明是如何运作的。

sents.en: For the defender, therefore, they are practically no different from infinitely many, and this is why this note treats the safety of a real system as a Π 1 \Pi_{1} statement.

sents.en: What matters in a real situation, then, is not whether the instances are finitely or infinitely many.
sents.zh: 于是，在真实情形中，重要的并不是实例是有限多个还是无限多个。

sents.en: It is whether the statement is settled by a single instance, as a Σ 1 \Sigma_{1} statement is, or only by something that covers all instances, as a Π 1 \Pi_{1} statement is.
sents.zh: 而是该命题是由单个实例就能判定（如 Σ_{1} 命题那样），还是只能由覆盖所有实例的东西来判定（如 Π_{1} 命题那样）。

sents.en: A list of checked instances, which is finite, covers all of them only if it is known to be complete, and in practice the defender’s list of checked states is never complete.

paragraphs.en: This shows that the division of labor between a statistical proposer and a deductive verifier is forced by what each of them can do, and not chosen by design. The proposer fixes the order in which candidates arrive, but it assures nothing, because it checks nothing. paragraphs.en: A reader may also ask how a finite proof can cover infinitely many inputs. It does not go through them one by one. The usual shape of a proof of 𝖲𝖺𝖿𝖾 ⁡ ( P ) \mathsf{Safe}(P) is an invariant, that is, a property of the states of P P that (i) holds in every initial state, (ii) is not destroyed by any step of P P , and (iii) excludes a violation. Each of (i) to (iii) is about a single state or a single step, so it can be established from the code of P P without following any run. Together they give 𝖲𝖺𝖿𝖾 ⁡ ( P ) \mathsf{Safe}(P) for every input and every number of steps, by induction on the number of steps. This is what Section 2 said: a finite derivation covers every run because a universal quantifier does, where no list of runs can. It is what verified software does ( Klein et al., 2009 ; Leroy, 2009 ) , and it is the direction taken by proposals for guaranteed safe AI ( Dalrymple et al., 2024 ) .
paragraphs.zh: 读者可能还会问：一个有限的证明如何能覆盖无穷多的输入。 它并不逐个遍历这些输入。 𝖲𝖺𝖿𝖾 ⁡ ( P ) \mathsf{Safe}(P) 的证明通常的形态是一个不变量，即 P P 的状态的一种性质，它 (i) 在每个初始状态都成立，(ii) 不会被 P P 的任何一步破坏，(iii) 排除违规的发生。 (i) 到 (iii) 的每一条都只涉及单个状态或单个步骤，因此可以直接从 P P 的代码加以确立，而无需追踪任何运行。 合在一起，通过对步数做归纳，它们就给出对每个输入和每个步数都成立的 𝖲𝖺𝖿𝖾 ⁡ ( P ) \mathsf{Safe}(P)。 这正是第 2 节所说的：一个有限的推导之所以能覆盖每一次运行，是因为全称量词能做到这一点，而任何运行清单都做不到。 这正是经过验证的软件所做的（Klein et al., 2009；Leroy, 2009），也是保障安全的 AI 的相关提议所采取的方向（Dalrymple et al., 2024）。

sents.zh: 读者可能还会问：一个有限的证明如何能覆盖无穷多的输入。

sents.en: It does not go through them one by one.
sents.zh: 它并不逐个遍历这些输入。

sents.en: The usual shape of a proof of 𝖲𝖺𝖿𝖾 ⁡ ( P ) \mathsf{Safe}(P) is an invariant, that is, a property of the states of P P that (i) holds in every initial state, (ii) is not destroyed by any step of P P , and (iii) excludes a violation.
sents.zh: 𝖲𝖺𝖿𝖾 ⁡ ( P ) \mathsf{Safe}(P) 的证明通常的形态是一个不变量，即 P P 的状态的一种性质，它 (i) 在每个初始状态都成立，(ii) 不会被 P P 的任何一步破坏，(iii) 排除违规的发生。

sents.en: Each of (i) to (iii) is about a single state or a single step, so it can be established from the code of P P without following any run.
sents.zh: (i) 到 (iii) 的每一条都只涉及单个状态或单个步骤，因此可以直接从 P P 的代码加以确立，而无需追踪任何运行。

sents.en: Together they give 𝖲𝖺𝖿𝖾 ⁡ ( P ) \mathsf{Safe}(P) for every input and every number of steps, by induction on the number of steps.
sents.zh: 合在一起，通过对步数做归纳，它们就给出对每个输入和每个步数都成立的 𝖲𝖺𝖿𝖾 ⁡ ( P ) \mathsf{Safe}(P)。

sents.en: This is what Section 2 said: a finite derivation covers every run because a universal quantifier does, where no list of runs can.

sents.en: It is what verified software does ( Klein et al., 2009 ; Leroy, 2009 ) , and it is the direction taken by proposals for guaranteed safe AI ( Dalrymple et al., 2024 ) .

paragraphs.en: Finding such a proof is itself a search for a witness, namely a proof p p with 𝖯𝗋𝖿 T ​ ( p , ⌜ ​ 𝖲𝖺𝖿𝖾 ​ ( P ) ​ ⌝ ) \mathsf{Prf}_{T}(p,\ulcorner\mathsf{Safe}(P)\urcorner) . So the search is on the Σ 1 \Sigma_{1} side of Turing’s Undecidability Theorem, and Proposition 1 applies to it as to any other search. It may fail, and no rule says when to stop. But when it succeeds, what it assures is the Π 1 \Pi_{1} statement 𝖲𝖺𝖿𝖾 ⁡ ( P ) \mathsf{Safe}(P) , and that is the only route to assurance of safety in the sense of Definition 1 . That route is not open for every program: it is closed for an unsafe program, since an exploit exists and will be found by whichever loop reaches it first, the defender’s tests or the attacker’s search. In July, the attacker’s search reached it first. It is closed for some safe programs, too, since some true Π 1 \Pi_{1} statements have no proof in T T . What follows for engineering is that a system that contains an agent should be built so that its safety has a proof before it is deployed, as verified software is built, and not built first and proved afterward. The rest of this section will assume that a proof of safety has been established, and asks where the risk then goes.

paragraphs.en: A proof of safety accepted by a verifier guarantees that the deployed system is safe only if the following four conditions hold: First, the verifier must be sound; otherwise the proof accepted by it may not be a proof in T T . Second, T T must be consistent; otherwise a statement proved in T T may be false. Third, the mathematical definitions 𝒟 math \mathcal{D}_{\mathrm{math}} must be adequate; otherwise 𝖲𝖺𝖿𝖾 ⁡ ( P ) \mathsf{Safe}(P) may be true without saying what is meant by safety. Fourth, the schema 𝒟 schema \mathcal{D}_{\mathrm{schema}} must be adequate; otherwise P P may be safe while the deployed system is not. The proof establishes none of these four conditions but rather depends on them. Accordingly, the risk moves to these four places. The first two, namely “the verifier is sound” and “ T T is consistent”, are again Π 1 \Pi_{1} statements, while the last two, about the adequacy of the mathematical definitions and the schema, are questions of another kind. The two events of July and October show each of the four.

paragraphs.en: Any proof of safety in security depends on these four conditions, whatever the program. The first three are required for any proof in mathematics as well. In both domains, the goal is truth and the assurance is a derivation. In mathematics, the accepted route to the truth of σ \sigma is a proof in a trusted theory, and the soundness of the verifier, the soundness of that theory (which amounts to its consistency for a Π 1 \Pi_{1} theorem), and the adequacy of its definitions are all carried as a shared background that is not re-examined for each theorem. In security, the same three are present, but the adequacy of the schema 𝒟 schema \mathcal{D}_{\mathrm{schema}} is also required because 𝒟 schema \mathcal{D}_{\mathrm{schema}} ties the model that was proved safe to the system that was deployed. The adequacy of the schema cannot be treated as background, because an adversary tests it on the deployed system.

paragraphs.en: A certificate shows that a derivation in T T exists only if it is issued by a verifier that accepts only those derivations in T T . A verifier with this property is called sound , and “the verifier is sound” is a Π 1 \Pi_{1} statement about a program because the verifier is itself a program. The soundness of a verifier must be kept apart from the soundness of the theory T T , the latter being the property that T T proves only true statements. Neither implies the other. A verifier can be sound while the theory implemented by it proves a false statement, and a theory can be sound while its implementation, the verifier, accepts a non-derivation.
paragraphs.zh: 证书表明，T T 中存在一个推导，当且仅当该证书由一个只接受 T T 中那些推导的验证器所签发。 具有这种性质的验证器被称为可靠的（sound），而「验证器是可靠的」是一个关于程序的 Π 1 \Pi_{1} 语句，因为验证器本身就是一个程序。 验证器的可靠性必须与理论 T T 的可靠性区分开来，后者是指 T T 只证明真语句这一性质。 两者互不蕴含。 一个验证器可以是可靠的，而由它实现的理论却证明了一个假语句；一个理论也可以是可靠的，而它的实现即验证器却接受了一个非推导。

paragraphs.en: The latter is what actually happened in Lean: Lean 4.32.1 fixed a soundness bug in the kernel that was found with the help of an OpenAI model, and Lean 4.34.0 fixed three soundness issues found by AI adversarial testing and reported by OpenAI, one of which an OpenAI agent turned into two distinct exploits deriving False ( Lean 4.32.1, 2026 ; Lean 4.34.0, 2026 ) . The October catalog is built on the toolchain released after those fixes, and the statement that the current kernel accepts nothing but derivations in the implemented theory is a Π 1 \Pi_{1} statement for which there is no certificate. This Π 1 \Pi_{1} statement is about the current kernel, which is a program, so it is of the same kind as safety itself and is handled in the same ways: by checking the certificate again with an independent verifier, by proving the kernel correct in a further theory, or by keeping the kernel small enough to be checked by humans. In an evaluation harness, the grader plays the verifier’s part, and in July the agents attacked the grader before they attacked anything else. A sandbox has no verifier, since it does not try to show that the program inside it is safe (Section 4.1 ). What it relies on is the monitor, and the July monitor had a path it did not mediate.
paragraphs.zh: 后者正是在 Lean 中实际发生的事情：Lean 4.32.1 修复了在 OpenAI 模型帮助下发现的内核可靠性漏洞，Lean 4.34.0 修复了由 AI 对抗性测试发现、并由 OpenAI 报告的三个可靠性问题，其中一个问题被一个 OpenAI 智能体转化成两个不同的、可以推导出 False 的漏洞利用（Lean 4.32.1, 2026；Lean 4.34.0, 2026）。 十月的目录建立在那些修复之后发布的工具链之上，而“当前内核只接受已实现理论中的推导”这一陈述是一个 Π₁ 陈述，它没有证书。 这个 Π₁ 陈述针对的是当前内核，而内核是一个程序，所以它与安全性本身属于同一类问题，可以用同样的方式处理：用一个独立的验证器再次检查证书，在一个更进一层的中证明内核是正确的，或者把内核保持得足够小以便由人工检查。 在评估环境中，评分器扮演着验证器的角色，而在七月，智能体们在攻击任何其他东西之前先攻击了评分器。 沙盒没有验证器，因为它并不试图证明其内部的程序是安全的（见 4.1 节）。 它依赖的是监控器，而七月的监控器存在一条它未曾介入的路径。

sents.en: The October catalog is built on the toolchain released after those fixes, and the statement that the current kernel accepts nothing but derivations in the implemented theory is a Π 1 \Pi_{1} statement for which there is no certificate.

sents.en: This Π 1 \Pi_{1} statement is about the current kernel, which is a program, so it is of the same kind as safety itself and is handled in the same ways: by checking the certificate again with an independent verifier, by proving the kernel correct in a further theory, or by keeping the kernel small enough to be checked by humans.

sents.en: In an evaluation harness, the grader plays the verifier’s part, and in July the agents attacked the grader before they attacked anything else.

But it does not yet show that the statement is true , which in general requires the soundness of T T . Note that, for a Π 1 \Pi_{1} theorem such as 𝖲𝖺𝖿𝖾 ⁡ ( P ) \mathsf{Safe}(P) , its truth requires only the consistency of T T , which is a weaker property than soundness. To see why, suppose that 𝖲𝖺𝖿𝖾 ⁡ ( P ) \mathsf{Safe}(P) is provable in T T but false. Since it is false, it has a counterexample, namely numbers x 0 x_{0} and s 0 s_{0} such that 𝖵𝗂𝗈𝗅 ⁡ ( P , x 0 , s 0 ) \mathsf{Viol}(P,x_{0},s_{0}) is true. The relation 𝖵𝗂𝗈𝗅 \mathsf{Viol} is decidable, and every true instance of a decidable relation is provable in T T because T T extends Robinson arithmetic and every true Σ 1 \Sigma_{1} sentence is provable in the latter. So 𝖵𝗂𝗈𝗅 ⁡ ( P , x 0 , s 0 ) \mathsf{Viol}(P,x_{0},s_{0}) is provable in T T , which implies that the negation of 𝖲𝖺𝖿𝖾 ⁡ ( P ) \mathsf{Safe}(P) is provable in it. Hence both the statement 𝖲𝖺𝖿𝖾 ⁡ ( P ) \mathsf{Safe}(P) and its negation are provable in T T , which means that T T is inconsistent.

paragraphs.en: So whether or not a safety statement proved in T T is true depends on the consistency of T T . But “ T T is consistent” is itself a Π 1 \Pi_{1} statement, and Gödel’s Second Incompleteness Theorem implies that no consistent theory that contains enough arithmetic can prove its own consistency. This limitation is unavoidable for us because any theory in which safety proofs are done, including Lean’s type theory, does contain enough arithmetic. The consistency of T T can be proved by a stronger theory, but then the consistency of the latter must be proved by a still stronger theory, and the regress does not end. So a proof of safety does not remove the dependence on an unproved Π 1 \Pi_{1} statement. It does replace one such statement with a better one: for each new program P P , 𝖲𝖺𝖿𝖾 ⁡ ( P ) \mathsf{Safe}(P) is a new Π 1 \Pi_{1} statement, whereas “ T T is consistent” is a single statement shared by every proof ever done in T T and studied on its own for a century. A Lean certificate depends on the same kind of condition, that is, on the consistency of Lean’s type theory when the theorem is Π 1 \Pi_{1} , and on its soundness otherwise.

The relation 𝖵𝗂𝗈𝗅 \mathsf{Viol} is defined on a model of execution, 𝖲𝖺𝖿𝖾 ⁡ ( P ) \mathsf{Safe}(P) is a statement of arithmetic, and a proof of 𝖲𝖺𝖿𝖾 ⁡ ( P ) \mathsf{Safe}(P) is a proof about the model. But the July escape did not happen in a model. It happened on servers. A proof about the model says something about the deployed system only if the deployed system can do nothing that cannot be done by the model, and that is a claim about the empirical world and not a statement of arithmetic. This is where the empirical definitions 𝒟 emp ​ ( t ) \mathcal{D}_{\mathrm{emp}}(t) of K&K enter.

paragraphs.en: As is explained in K&K, 𝒟 emp ​ ( t ) \mathcal{D}_{\mathrm{emp}}(t) has two parts: a schema 𝒟 schema \mathcal{D}_{\mathrm{schema}} and a record of facts 𝒟 fact ​ ( t ) \mathcal{D}_{\mathrm{fact}}(t) . The part that matters here is the schema. The record plays no part, because the proof of 𝖲𝖺𝖿𝖾 ⁡ ( P ) \mathsf{Safe}(P) uses no recorded fact about the system, and a safety argument that did rely on such facts would be an argument from tests, which has already been treated in Section 4.1 . The schema fixes which fact of the world is represented by each symbol of the model. For the sandbox, it fixes which channels of the deployed system count as the inputs x x of 𝖵𝗂𝗈𝗅 ⁡ ( P , x , s ) \mathsf{Viol}(P,x,s) and which events count as a violation. This must be laid down explicitly, because mathematics alone does not say anything about it. paragraphs.en: This note is based on known results: Turing’s Undecidability Theorem, the reduction from the halting set behind Corollary 1 , Church’s result behind Corollary 2 , the notion of a safety property ( Lamport, 1977 ; Alpern and Schneider, 1985 ) , Dijkstra’s remark on testing ( Dijkstra, 1970 ) , the exploit as a witness ( Clarke et al., 1999 ; Avgerinos et al., 2011 ) , the arithmetical hierarchy as a classification of what can be verified and what can be refuted ( Kelly, 1996 ) , and the undecidability of containment ( Alfonseca et al., 2021 ) . Our hybrid framework puts them under a single definition of assurance. Under it, the agents that breached Hugging Face and the agents that produced Lean proofs of a zero-free region for ζ \zeta were doing the same kind of thing, although the two domains differ in the statement each one wants. We hope that this analysis is of use for what agentic AI faces next: proofs of safety for the systems that contain agents, and a clear view of where the risk remains once such a proof has been obtained.

paragraphs.en: For each index e e let P e P_{e} be the program that, on input x x , first simulates machine e e on the empty tape and, if the simulation halts, then behaves as Q Q on x x . The map e ↦ P e e\mapsto P_{e} is computable. If e ∈ 𝖧𝖺𝗅𝗍 e\in\mathsf{Halt} the simulation halts, and P e P_{e} then violates φ \varphi on the input on which Q Q does, after a larger number of steps, by the second part of the second hypothesis, so P e ∈ 𝖴𝗇𝗌𝖺𝖿𝖾 P_{e}\in\mathsf{Unsafe} . If e ∉ 𝖧𝖺𝗅𝗍 e\notin\mathsf{Halt} the simulation never halts, and by the first part of the second hypothesis no violation occurs, so P e ∉ 𝖴𝗇𝗌𝖺𝖿𝖾 P_{e}\notin\mathsf{Unsafe} .
